title: Chicago Man Charged With Killing Estranged Wife, Arrested at O'Hare While Fleeing to India
excerpt: Prosecutors say Ankur Patel, 31, lured his estranged wife to Chicago with a promise she could see their daughter — after secretly sending the child to India — then tried to board a flight out of O'Hare.
body:
• Ankur Patel, 31, of Chicago has been charged with first-degree murder in the August stabbing death of his estranged wife, prosecutors told a Cook County court.
  • Prosecutors allege Patel lured the woman to Chicago by promising she could see their five-year-old daughter, after secretly sending the child to live with his parents in India.
  • He was arrested at O'Hare International Airport the day after the killing as he tried to board a flight to India, after Homeland Security was alerted.
  • Patel remains in custody. The charges are allegations presented by prosecutors and have not been proven in court.

A 31-year-old Chicago man of Indian origin has been charged with first-degree murder after prosecutors told a court he lured his estranged wife to Chicago with a promise she could see their young daughter, stabbed her to death, and then tried to flee the United States for India. Ankur Patel was arrested at O'Hare International Airport and remains in custody as the case proceeds, according to the prosecution account reported by Times Now World and Aviation A2Z.

A Marriage That Had Broken Down

According to prosecutors, the woman, whose name has not been released, left Patel in May and began dating a former colleague. Under pressure from family members, she briefly gave the marriage another chance and moved back in with him in Wisconsin, but left again soon afterward, leaving their five-year-old daughter in Patel's care and moving to Louisiana with her new partner.

Prosecutors alleged that Patel then threatened to kill both his estranged wife and her new partner over the phone, and stopped allowing the woman to speak with her daughter.

The Daughter Was Already in India

About two weeks before the killing in August, prosecutors said, Patel moved in with relatives in Chicago and sent his daughter to live with his parents in India, without telling his estranged wife. He then invited her to Chicago on the pretext that she could meet the child. She drove to Chicago with her new partner, who waited outside the apartment building, unaware the girl was no longer in the country.

Investigators said surveillance footage from a store showed Patel buying a small folding knife in the days before the meeting, and appeared to show him making stabbing and slicing motions. Assistant State's Attorney Mike Pekara told the court that footage captured the couple arguing, and that Patel then attacked the woman with the knife, inflicting a fatal wound to her neck. An autopsy found multiple defensive injuries, including a deep laceration to her left arm.

Arrested at O'Hare

The woman's partner, waiting outside, called 911 when she stopped responding to messages, but officers who attended could not identify which apartment she had entered and left. Her body was found later that evening by acquaintances of Patel who went to the apartment after he failed to show up for a planned meeting.

By then Patel was at O'Hare. Prosecutors said the ticket counters were closed when he first arrived, so he checked into a nearby hotel and disposed of the knife, then bought new shoes and clothing at a Target store the next day before returning to the airport and buying a ticket to India. The Department of Homeland Security had been alerted, and he was arrested before he could leave the country.

According to the account of his police interview, Patel told investigators he had not intended to kill his wife, but acted after she confirmed she would not return to him and intended to remain with her new partner.

What Happens Next

Patel faces a first-degree murder charge and remains in custody while legal proceedings continue. The account above is the prosecution's case as presented in court; the allegations have not been tested at trial. The couple's five-year-old daughter remains in India with Patel's parents.
